summary.text: Nupe was a river power with horses. Its Kede canoemen ruled the middle Niger, and its cavalry raided the Yoruba and the confluence; under the emirs of Bida (from 1857) it became one of the strongest raiding states of the caliphate.

arms.text: The Kede canoemen controlled traffic on the middle Niger.
Horsemen carried Nupe’s raids south and west.
The Bida emirate raised large cavalry armies for its raids on Okun and the confluence.
Guns came with the river trade in the late 19th century.

record.text: Nupe armies sacked Oyo-Ile and drove its court into exile.
Alaafin Abiodun’s army was destroyed in Nupe, losing the equivalent of thirteen generals.
Nupe raids took the confluence lands from Igala rule.
Esan tradition says the Akota alliance drove the Nupe back to Agbede after three years.
Bida’s cavalry camped at Ogidi and the allies held their hill; the war was still open when the Company came.
The Company’s force with Maxim guns took Bida.
